governanceNotes: D1 batch 73 (2026-09-26): posterior-tibial-tendon-dysfunction DEFERRED without edges - IDENTITY-OVERLAP (PCFD consensus unification) plus CONSTITUTIVE-PROXIMITY plus below-threshold quantification. Searched anchors: the 2020 consensus overview (PMID 40523163) documenting that posterior tibial tendon dysfunction and adult acquired flatfoot deformity are traditional terminologies for one progressive collapsing foot deformity construct; the instructional review (PMID 42257901) documenting PTT failure and ligament attenuation as the biomechanical drivers with Johnson and Strom staging (stage II defined by the flexible deformity); the MR imaging review (PMID 42442878) documenting AAFD as a progressive condition whose key findings include posterior tibial tendon dysfunction; the acute-rupture case report (PMID 41171964) documenting rapid development of progressive collapsing foot deformity after tendon rupture (case-report class); and the cadaveric biomechanics study (PMID 42790184) documenting posterior tibial tendon unloading effects across progressive ligamentous failure (cadaver model, not clinical evidence). The located literature measures the deformity construct itself - staging, imaging, and biomechanics - rather than a quantified incidence of flatfoot as a separate downstream condition, and the consensus framing treats tendon dysfunction and deformity as one disease, so an edge would register the defining feature as a secondary condition (constitutive-proximity, piriformis batch-71 precedent). Reopening: a natural-history cohort of deformity-free stage-I PTTD, or catalog-scope validation separating the flatfoot identity from PTTD-driven acquired deformity. Chain-disclosure: the published flatfoot to osteoarthritis edge is left untouched and a PTTD to osteoarthritis edge is withheld so no chain triangle is introduced.
